intro.title: Org Settings → Finance
lines: Everything that controls how money maps to your accounting lives here,
grouped into GL Library, Accounting, and Transaction Rules.
We'll click into each section.
intro.narration: Welcome to the Finance section of the Rec admin, under Org Settings. This is where everything that controls how money maps to your accounting system lives. It's organized into three groups: the GL Library, Accounting, and Transaction Rules. Let's click into each one.

steps.title: GL Library · Chart of Accounts
lines: Your master list of GL accounts — each has a name and a GL code.
These are referenced throughout the accounting system.
Search, add, archive, or export accounts from here.
steps.narration: First, the GL Library. The Chart of Accounts is your master list of general ledger accounts. Each account has a name and a GL code, and these are referenced throughout the accounting system. From here you can search, add, archive, or export accounts.

steps.title: Accounting · Default Accounts
lines: The fallback GL accounts journal entries post to.
Standard revenue splits by payment method — Credit Card, Cash, Check.
Also account-credit, security-deposit, tax and transaction-fee accounts.
steps.narration: Under Accounting, Default Accounts sets the fallback GL accounts that journal entries post to. Standard revenue is split by payment method — credit card, cash, and check — and refunds post back as credits. You'll also set the accounts for account credit, security deposits, tax, and transaction fees here.

steps.title: Accounting · General Ledger
lines: Org-wide revenue-recognition rules, one set per revenue type.
Each row is tagged Purchase or Service Delivery.
The second video walks through these in detail.
steps.narration: Next, the General Ledger. These are your organization-wide revenue recognition rules, one set per revenue type. Each row is tagged either Purchase or Service Delivery, showing when its revenue is recognized. We'll cover these in depth in the second video.

steps.title: Transaction Rules · Tax
lines: Choose the GL code for tax — inherit it from each tax item,
or apply one global GL code across all taxable transactions.
steps.narration: In Transaction Rules, the Tax page controls the GL code used for tax. You can inherit the code from each individual tax item, or apply one global GL code across all taxable transactions.

steps.title: Transaction Rules · Processing Fee
lines: The processing fee on online payments (edited by support),
and the GL code it posts to.
steps.narration: Processing Fee sets the fee charged on online payments. The percentage itself is managed by customer support, but you choose the GL code it posts to right here.

steps.title: Transaction Rules · Ticket Service Fee
lines: Toggle whether the 2% ticket service fee (min $0.50) is passed to
customers or absorbed by the org — and set its GL code.
steps.narration: Ticket Service Fee lets you decide whether the two percent ticket service fee, with a fifty cent minimum, is passed on to customers at checkout or absorbed by your organization. You also set the GL code it posts to.

steps.title: Transaction Rules · Desk Location
lines: Require staff to select a desk location before taking a payment —
useful for reconciling cash drawers by location.
steps.narration: Desk Location, when enabled, requires staff to select a desk location before processing any payment. That's useful for reconciling cash drawers by location.

steps.title: Transaction Rules · Price Override
lines: Require staff to enter a reason and note whenever they override a price.
steps.narration: And Price Override prompts staff to enter a reason and a note whenever they override a price, so every change is documented.
